verses.1: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and thirty-one years he reigned in Jerusalem.
verses.2: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the ways of David his father, not turning to the right or to the left.
verses.3: In the eighth year of his reign, and he still a youth, he began to seek the God of David his father, and in the twelfth year of his reign he began to purify Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, the Asherim, and the carved images.
verses.4: He tore down the altars of the Baals that were before him, and the high places that were on them, and he cut down the Asherim and the carved images; he broke them and crushed them, and scattered them on the faces of the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
verses.5: He burned the bones of the priests on the altars, and so he purified Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.6: And in the cities of Ephraim and Manasseh and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, in all their territories around.
verses.7: He tore down the altars and the shrines, and beat the images into dust, and broke down all the high places throughout the land of Israel, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.8: In the eighteenth year of his reign, to purify the land and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the scribe, to strengthen the house of the LORD his God.
verses.9: They came to Hilkiah the high priest, and gave him the silver brought into the house of God, which the Levites, the gatekeepers, had gathered from the hands of Manasseh and Ephraim and all the remnant of Israel and Judah and Benjamin and the residents of Jerusalem.
verses.10: They gave it to those who did the work, the overseers in the house of the LORD, and they gave it to those who did the work in the house of the LORD, to repair and strengthen the house.
verses.11: They gave it to the craftsmen and builders, to buy hewn stones and timber for joining the houses that the kings of Judah had destroyed.
verses.12: The men worked faithfully in their tasks, and over them were overseers: Jahath and Obadiah the Levites, from the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the sons of the Kohathites, to oversee, and all the Levites who had knowledge of musical instruments.
verses.13: Over the bearers and all who did the work, there were laborers and overseers from the Levites, scribes, gatekeepers, and guards.
verses.14: When they brought out the silver that had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the Law of the LORD in the hand of Moses.
verses.15: Hilkiah answered Shaphan the scribe, saying, “I have found the book of the Law in the house of the LORD.” And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
verses.16: Shaphan brought the book to the king, and read it to the king, saying, “All that was given into the hands of your servants they are doing.”
verses.17: They gave the silver found in the house of the LORD to those in charge and to those doing the work.
verses.18: Shaphan the scribe told the king, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book.” And Shaphan read it before the king.
verses.19: When the king heard the words of the Law, he tore his robes.
verses.20: He commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Abdon the son of Micah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant, saying:
verses.21: “Go, seek the LORD on my behalf, and on behalf of the remnant in Israel and Judah, because of the words of the book that was found. For the anger of the LORD is great against us, because our ancestors did not keep the word of the LORD, to do according to all that is written in this book.”
verses.22: Hilkiah and those the king had sent went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Takath, the son of Harhas, who was in charge of the garments, and she lived in Jerusalem in the second district. They spoke with her about this.
verses.23: She said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, say to the man who sent you to me:
verses.24: Thus says the LORD: I am bringing evil upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the words written in the book that was read before the king of Judah.
verses.25: Because they have forsaken me and burned incense to other gods, to provoke me with all the works of their hands, and my anger will burn against this place and will not be quenched.”
verses.26: And to the king of Judah, who sent you to seek the LORD, say this to him: “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: The words you have heard
verses.27: your heart has been softened and you have humbled yourself before me when you heard my words about this place and its inhabitants, and you have humbled yourself before me and torn your robes and wept before me. And I have heard,” says the LORD.
verses.28: “Behold, I will gather you to your ancestors and you will be gathered to your tombs in peace, and your eyes will not see all the evil that I am bringing upon this place and its inhabitants.” And they returned to the king the word.
verses.29: The king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.30: The king went up to the house of the LORD, and all the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem, and the priests and the Levites and all the people, from the greatest to the least. He read to their ears all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the LORD.
verses.31: The king stood on the stand and made a covenant before the LORD to walk after the LORD and to keep his commandments, his testimonies, and his statutes with all his heart and all his soul, to do the words of the covenant written in this book.
verses.32: He set all who were found in Jerusalem and Benjamin to do so, and the residents of Jerusalem made a covenant with the God of their ancestors.
verses.33: Josiah removed all the abominations from all the lands belonging to the sons of Israel, and made all who were found in Israel to serve the LORD their God all the days of his life. He did not turn from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

notes:
Notes
- v. 14: "the book of the Law of the LORD in the hand of Moses" – This is a direct translation of "סֵפֶר תּוֹרַת־יְהוָה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה" (the book of the Law of the LORD in the hand of Moses). The reference to Moses here likely indicates that the book is associated with the teachings attributed to him, even if the text itself is newly discovered.
